survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Albania using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The note describes that PISA assesses 15-year-olds through complex sampling across 81 participating countries/economies and that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (asterisk) requiring caution. The factsheet itself does not specify which student sampling weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) was applied in the production of the published estimates. For analysts using the underlying PISA database, the appropriate complex survey weights and replicate procedures should be applied as recommended in the PISA Reader’s Guide and technical documentation; this factsheet does not provide those implementation details.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical analysis paper that models outcomes with a specified PV-based dependent variable. It reports published mean performance trends and questionnaire percentages, but it does not document a PV estimation or combining procedure (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or any explicit missing-data handling method for an analytic model. Therefore, plausible values handling and missing-data handling are not reported in the factsheet text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the Albania analytic participation figures for PISA 2022: 6,129 students in 274 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science. No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade restrictions beyond PISA’s 15-year-old target, item-completion thresholds, or missing-data exclusions) are specified in the factsheet; it presents the country participation counts as reported in the OECD PISA 2022 Database.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Albania factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Albania performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how they reported on engagement, belonging, safety, and parental involvement. It explains that PISA 2022 used two two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different item sets, and that results are released for mathematics, reading, and science (with creative thinking and financial literacy as additional/optional components). The factsheet reports that average results in Albania declined in 2022 compared to 2018 across mathematics, reading, and science, and it highlights that students reported spending significantly less effort in 2022 than in 2018, with indications of low engagement requiring cautious interpretation. It also provides contextual indicators: students’ sense of belonging and life satisfaction declined, while reported teacher support in mathematics lessons remained relatively high. The note further contextualizes the decline with disruptions from the 2019 earthquake and COVID-19-related schooling interruptions.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical study estimating a predictive model. As such, it does not provide an ML pipeline, target-variable definitions for modeling, or reported PV/missing-data handling procedures, and it does not report model performance metrics. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and focuses on the assessment design and reported descriptive outcomes.
